taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station T-01 (survey area T). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1056.4 | 23.97 | 23.97
2 | 1090.4 | 1.46 | 25.43
3 | 2606.8 | 3.17 | 28.60
4 | 3560.6 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as HA-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Station: T-01
Curve type: A-type (resistivity rises continuously with depth: 1056.4 → 1090.4 → 2606.8 → 3560.6 Ω·m). Note: this contradicts the "HA" label on file — an H-type first branch requires ρ1 > ρ2, which is not the case here; the curve should be re-classified as ascending (A/AA) type.
Aquifer depth: approx. 0–25.4 m (Layers 1–2, the comparatively lower-resistivity weathered zone above the sharp resistivity rise at 28.6 m)
Recommendation: Target drilling through the weathered/fractured interval down to about 25–28 m, where resistivity is lowest and fracture-hosted groundwater is most likely; the underlying high-resistivity layer (>2600 Ω·m) likely represents compact, low-yield bedrock, so drilling deeper than ~30 m is unlikely to improve yield and should be reassessed before proceeding.
